title: Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra" (ASSi): cipher letters of the 15th-16th c., with the 43 filed keys of fasc. 1 (DECODE R4746-R4814, R1858)

system.summary: A corpus: each letter uses its own Sienese or foreign key of the period (homophonic substitution with nulls, doubles and a small nomenclator), so the system is per document.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments or glosses on some pieces (nos. 8, 10, 13/16); DECODE R1858 marked Decrypted; the 1952 inventory calls the letters 'solo parzialmente decifrate'

conditions.human_role: Set the goal (decipher the 29 letters; try the 42 filed keys first). Instructed that DECODE records marked Decrypted are to be trusted as read.

solution.what: Found the whole busta Concistoro 2308 on DECODE (keys R4746-R4789, letters R4790-R4814, R1858), missed by the 23 Sept scan; downloaded 131 images with the project cookie.
Inventoried fasc. 2 by the pencil numbers (Meister's numbering: no. 4 = 1456, no. 11 = 1478, no. 17 = 1528 hold). Nos. 1 (the 1421 letter), 2, 26-28 are not among the 25 pieces photographed.

Viewed and indexed the 43 key records (1433 Petrucci, c. 1440 frate Bernardino, 1454 Milan ambassadors, Casole, 1478 Bichi, c. 1500 Valentino/Pandolfo keys, 1502, 1536, 1540s Tosta, 16th-c. code books).
No. 8 (c. 1440): ciphered slip with its contemporary decipherment on the same sheet; no. 10: glossed letter by letter 'presura di Montepulciano'; no. 13: decipherment filed as no. 16.

Senatore 2009 (Callisto III nelle corrispondenze diplomatiche, Revista Borja 2) cites 'una lettera in cifra di Borghesi a Benvoglienti ... Concistoro 2308, c. 4 (da Napoli, 12 maggio [1456])' and lists Concistoro 2308 as 'lettere cifrate e cifrari di ambasciatori'; no decipherment printed. Treccani DBI Borghese: none.

Compared by eye the alphabets of the 1450s keys R4750 (Milan ambassadors 1454, same Latin code-word family: 'storpsi' = ambasciatore fiorentino), R4753, R4754, R4756, R4762 with the signs of no. 4 (1456): none produces its letters.
Transcribed the unnumbered all-cipher slip R4794 (170 tokens, 38 glyphs, numbers 44, 26, 67, 74 as code groups) from an automatic glyph-segmentation sheet.
Homophonic simulated annealing (homsolve.py, it-cinquecento and la order-4 LMs, unigram KL prior) on R4794: no convergence, restarts disagree.
Subagent transcriptions of no. 6 (1,056 tokens, 65 sign names, continuous) and no. 17 (286 tokens, 42 sign names, 1528, to Antonio del Vescovo, 'questa cifra è quella di Balìa').

Homophonic annealing on no. 6, 8 restarts x 200k iterations, Italian and Latin: no convergence (-2.66 / -2.64 per char, gibberish); IC x types 1.93, few repeats beyond trigrams ('p p W' 7x, 'SS 3 W' 5x).

Checked the alphabets of the 16th-c. keys R4760 (1536), R4765, R4767 (Aglo Venturi), R4768 (Mercanto, lowercase-letter cipher with nulls e g f h k 8 6), R4775 (1502), R4778, R4779, R4785 against nos. 17, 20 and R4794: no match seen.
No. 14 (R4802) transcribed by a subagent: ~1,300 tokens, 248 point-divided words; re-checked to split the sign OBAR into OL/OR/O after key work showed it stood for both d and m.
wordsolve.py (spaced it-cinquecento LM, order 4/5, 10 x 300k) on no. 14 without cribs: stuck on pseudo-Italian.

Hand crib on the recurring words '8 6 RR IB VB Q' = nostra/vostra, 'RR IB EQ IB 6' = stato, 'Y 6 RR IB VB' = vostr-: re-anneal gives Italian ('del nostro stato e dela nostra cita', 'considerano', 'carlo', 'toscana').
homsolve2.py (staged order 3->4 anneal, frequency-seeded restarts, swap moves) on no. 14 with NO crib reaches the same key and better score (-3991 on the corrected transcription).

No. 20 (R4808) transcribed by a subagent: 1,231 tokens, 51 sign names, continuous; clear opening 'Sacra Regia Maiestas ... ante terre pedum oscula', closing 'Scriptum Perusii(?) die penultimo mensis Martii'.
No. 20: homsolve.py Italian/Latin, with and without f/o^n as nulls, and with f as word divider; homsolve2.py Latin: no convergence.
No. 11 (Acciaiuoli 1478, 409 tokens, 44 signs, 'PLUS O' merged): homophonic anneal Italian, no convergence.
